PSS network projections

Generated by docs/projection_figures.py (skm-pss-adapters v0.2.0-2-g2e66d8b) on 2026-10-12, from 786 reactions (access: public, species: ath).

The Plant Stress Signalling (PSS) knowledge graph is made of curated reactions. For analysis, each reaction is turned into (projected onto) three networks:

  • reaction graph: reactions and their participants as nodes, with edges from each participant to the reaction (input, activator, inhibitor) and from the reaction to its outputs;
  • interaction network: entities only (proteins, complexes, metabolites, …), with entity → entity edges that have an influence: positive, negative or unknown;
  • gene network: the interaction network with each gene cluster replaced by its genes.

This document shows, with examples from the data: (1) how each reaction type is projected, (2) how reactions connect to each other in the interaction network, and (3) the skm-tools functions that simplify the interaction network. The legend below applies to all figures.

Conditions (e.g. "NPR1 high & JAZ low", modifiers of many transcriptional reactions) appear only in the reaction graph: the interaction and gene networks leave them out.

Self-loops. An entity that is both an input and an output of a reaction (e.g. the protein in a protein activation, which is not split into an inactive and an active node) gives no edge. The only self-loops are autoregulation: a modifier that regulates its own production, e.g. a transcription factor activating its own transcription (see the last figure of section 1).

1. Projections of each reaction type

One example reaction for each reaction type and effect, drawn in the three networks: the reaction graph, the interaction network and the gene network (species: ath). Nodes are in the same place in each: inputs above, outputs below, activators right, inhibitors left. In the gene network, the genes of a gene cluster are drawn around the cluster's name.

The table above each figure lists the rules that make the interaction network edges for that reaction type: from which participants to which, with which influence. substrates are the inputs, products the outputs and modifiers the activators and inhibitors (activating_modifiers and inhibiting_modifiers when the two are treated differently). directed edges go one way; mutual edges link each pair of participants in both directions.

2. How reactions chain in the interaction network

Reactions connect when an entity made by one reaction (upstream) is used by another (downstream), as an input or a modifier. This section shows, for each reaction type, its 3 most common downstream connections, each with one example pair of reactions drawn in the interaction network. The shared entity is outlined in orange, and edges are labelled with their reaction id and type.

The table lists all connections: the upstream reaction type, the downstream reaction type, the role of the shared entity in the downstream reaction, the number of reaction pairs connected this way, and an example (upstream reaction, shared entity, downstream reaction). The counts are also in chains/chains.tsv.
